# Rate Content

> Score a piece against stated criteria, with a quote behind every score.

## Done means
- Criteria are named and defined before scoring, and the definition says what full marks look like.
- Every score cites evidence from the piece. A score with no quote is an impression.
- Scores are independent; a strong thesis does not lift the evidence score.
- The verdict follows the scores arithmetically, and any override is justified explicitly.
- The single most valuable improvement is named.

## Output contract
```
## Criteria
| criterion | full marks looks like |
## Scores
| criterion | score /5 | evidence (quote) |
## Verdict
<overall, and who this is worth reading for>
## The one change
```

Default criteria for written work are novelty, evidence, clarity, usefulness, honesty about uncertainty. Swap them when the piece has a different job.

## Gotchas
Do not reward length, confidence, or polish. A well-written piece with no evidence scores low on evidence and high on clarity, and the table should show exactly that.
